stories.title: U.S.-Canada trade talks collapse just before deadline for tariffs
stories.summary: The midnight deadline means that U.S. will impose 50% tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian products. Prime Minister Mark Carney says Canada "will match those tariffs dollar for dollar."

stories.title: France's Fontainebleau forest reopens one month after wilfire
stories.summary: Good news for hiking and climbing enthusiasts today: the Fontainebleau Forest just South of Paris is set to reopen to the public. But a month and a half after the terrible fire that ravaged 10% of this unique haven of biodiversity, the disaster is still fresh in everyone’s minds. Portions of the forest remain closed to the public. Story by France 2 and Camille Corcoran.

stories.title: Trump frames upcoming midterms as battle to defeat communists who he says never laugh
stories.summary: US President said he has never seen a happy communist
article_sentences: US President Donald Trump said he has never seen a happy communist.
There're very unhappy people," the US leader told his supporters at a rally in Myrtle Beach, a city in South Carolina, on Friday.
Trump also pledged to defeat what he called a growing communist threat from the Democratic Party at the midterms in November.
In his speech, Trump said he would be happy if rules were changed to allow him a third run.

stories.title: Maradona's 'Hand of God' ball in match against England goes for auction
stories.summary: The football that Diego Maradona punched into the net for his infamous "Hand of God" goal is under the hammer this weekend. The historic ball from that infamous quarter final World Cup match between Argentina and England in 1986 is expected to fetch over 10 million dollars. Details by Camille Knight.

stories.title: Germany’s top diplomat arrives in Kiev on unannounced visit
stories.summary: Johann Wadephul's agenda includes meetings to discuss assistance to Ukraine and bilateral cooperation in security
article_sentences: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul arrived in Kiev on an unannounced visit on Saturday.
His agenda includes meetings to discuss assistance to Ukraine and bilateral cooperation in security, Germany’s MFA said.
The visit comes ahead of Independence Day of Ukraine celebrated on August 24, the German Foreign Ministry specified.
"The visit will mostly center on preparations for the winter.

Among other things, these include supplying generators, spare parts and other energy equipment, support to the Ukrainian energy sector, and also measures to protect critical infrastructure," Germany’s diplomatic agency specified.

In addition, Wadephul will discuss "deepening cooperation with Ukraine in the sphere of defense and security, mostly in bolstering military capabilities, exchanging experience, and jointly producing long-term security structures."
The minister arrived in Kiev by rail.
The trip was not announced for security reasons.
This is Wadephul’s fourth visit to Ukraine as Germany’s Foreign Minister.
